scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): backs taking student interests into account while insisting educators decide what students need; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Lessons come alive when they connect to what students actually care about.
Some people recommend that educators should take students' interests into account when planning the content of their courses.
I agree that student interests should shape teaching, but I believe educators must still decide what students truly need to learn.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why interests should shape teaching

sentences.text: First, paying attention to students' interests can make learning far more effective.
Students who find a topic interesting concentrate harder and remember much more of it.
For example, a history class built around questions students chose often sparks lively discussion.
This shows that connecting lessons to real interests can deepen both attention and understanding.
Considering interests also shows respect for students and makes them partners in their own learning.
A teacher who knows what excites her class can explain ideas in ways that genuinely reach them.
To this extent, taking interests into account is clearly wise.
Second, however, student interests cannot be the only thing that shapes a course.
Young learners often do not yet know which skills will matter most in their later lives.
Consider a class that would gladly skip difficult writing or mathematics that it will later badly need.
Following interest alone in such cases would leave dangerous gaps in students' knowledge.
Educators have the experience to see the whole journey of learning that students cannot yet see.
Some essential subjects become interesting only after the hard early stages are passed.
Interests, then, should guide a course without ever fully controlling it.
In conclusion, educators are right to take students' interests into account when planning lessons.
But they must still ensure that students learn what they truly need for the future.
The best teaching joins genuine student interest with the steady guidance only an educator can give.
